correctness.rationale: Phase rigidity follows from distinct cyclic rotations of a primitive root. At length below the period all one-letter extensions repeat; long occurrences occupy one residue class modulo the period. Positive phases repeat their left extension, while zero-phase classes of size >=3 repeat a left/right extension; the unique surviving class is exactly the two copies of the (e-1)-fold root at the text boundaries. Boundary and exponent-two witness explicitly checked. Two independent computational methods passed 2679 and 1154 finite cases; the analytic proof establishes universal quantifiers.

value.rationale: Net frequency is an established context-sensitive repetition invariant used in compressed string analysis. This completes its full factor-by-factor spectrum, including precise positions, for the natural all-alphabet, all-primitive-root periodic family and proves the sharp universal cube threshold. It resolves a structural boundary distinct from ad hoc small tests or routine substitutions of a known bound; the exact two-occurrence collapse and square counterexample explain why genuine periodicity differs from morphic special cases.
